root_cause.text: Ceph’s lookup/finish-lookup paths in `fs/ceph/dir.c` incorrectly assumed that a negative dentry was safe to pass to `d_add()` even when it was already hashed in the dcache, causing `__d_rehash()` to reinsert the same `dentry->d_hash` node and corrupt the hlist bucket.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes both `ceph_finish_lookup()` and `ceph_lookup()` from unconditional `d_add(dentry, NULL);` to `if (d_unhashed(dentry)) d_add(dentry, NULL);`, and the CVE text states that “re-adding an already-hashed negative dentry” can corrupt the bucket and make `__d_lookup()` spin forever.

intent_record.intent_summary: Only add the dentry to the dcache when it is still unhashed, preventing duplicate or inconsistent dentry handling in Ceph lookup completion.
intent_record.what: In ceph_finish_lookup(), the unconditional call to d_add(dentry, NULL) in the non-error path was replaced with a conditional that only calls d_add() when dentry is unhashed: if (d_unhashed(dentry)) d_add(dentry, NULL);
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents re-adding a dentry that is already hashed/attached in the dcache, while still adding unhashed dentries as before. It avoids duplicate dentry insertion or incorrect dcache state during lookup completion.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix Ceph lookup completion so a dentry is only added to the dcache when it is still unhashed, avoiding duplicate or inconsistent negative dentry insertion.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: they prevent Ceph lookup/finish-lookup from calling d_add() on a negative dentry that is already hashed, avoiding duplicate dentry insertion and dcache corruption.

candidates.rationale: This is the unsafe negative-dentry insertion that could be reached even when the dentry was already hashed, leading to duplicate rehashing of the same dentry->d_hash node and dcache corruption.
This lookup-completion path also unconditionally added a negative dentry, which is the direct behavior implicated by the root cause when the dentry was already present in the dcache.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line unconditionally inserts a negative dentry into the dcache during Ceph lookup completion. As described in the root cause, doing so when the dentry is already hashed can cause __d_rehash() to operate on an already-linked d_hash node, corrupting the hlist bucket.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in this snippet: `ceph_finish_lookup()` unconditionally calls `d_add(dentry, NULL);` on the ENOENT/no-trace path when `dentry->d_inode` is NULL: `if (dentry->d_inode) { d_drop(dentry); ... } else { d_add(dentry, NULL); }`. The root cause says Ceph incorrectly assumed a negative dentry was safe to pass to `d_add()` even when it was already hashed, which could trigger `__d_rehash()` corruption. This code shows exactly that unsafe pattern and there is no guarding check for `d_unhashed(dentry)` or any equivalent fix, so the fix is not present in this commit.
